clue.text: Forcefully take responsibility for emergency room for motorists?

parts.note: to do something hard is to do it with force
to shoulder a burden is to accept responsibility for it

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to seize control of a hospital's emergency room, with a question mark hinting at a twist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Emergency room' looks medical, but it means space to stop in an emergency. The hard shoulder is the strip beside a British motorway where broken-down cars pull over.
explanation.definitionFit: The paved verge beside a motorway exists so drivers in trouble have a safe place to stop.

clue.text: Small house rented back as temporary accommodation

parts.note: HO is the short form of house

indicators.note: back tells us the word for rented is written backwards

parts.note: property that is rented has been let

explanation.surface: A little cottage let out serves as a stopgap place to live.
explanation.definitionFit: Guests stay a night or a few at an inn-style establishment, so it is short-term lodging.

clue.text: Port in great quantity sent left by brother and I

indicators.note: in an across answer, sending a word left makes it run from right to left

parts.note: lots means a great quantity

explanation.surface: A sibling and the speaker ship a huge consignment out of a harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent left' means written right to left, as an across answer reads backwards; 'in' and 'by' just join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Bristol, in south-west England, is a historic harbour city on the Avon.

clue.text: Belt or sock as things to wear

definitions.meaning: both are informal words for hitting someone hard
British slang for clothes and gear

explanation.surface: A belt or a sock both count as items of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Belt and sock look like garments, which the second definition encourages, but here they are verbs meaning to strike.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for striking heavily and British slang for clothing, two unrelated senses.

clue.text: Positions taken by speakers backing relief work

indicators.note: backing means the combined words are read in reverse order

parts.note: aid is relief given to those in need
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Speakers take positions in support of aid work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' looks like support, but it reverses AIDOP.
explanation.definitionFit: Lecturers and orators stand on raised platforms; this is the Latin-style plural.

clue.text: Old man's attempt to make dough

parts.note: the old man is father, so pa's
an attempt is a try

explanation.surface: Dad tries his hand at making money, or bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dough' suggests money, but it is the baker's mixture.
explanation.definitionFit: Flour, fat and water mixed into a paste for pies is a kind of baking dough.

clue.text: Mark of distinction long observed in court

indicators.note: observed in says one word is seen sitting inside another

parts.note: to long for something is to ache for it

explanation.surface: An honour that has long been noticed in a royal court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'long' is a verb, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Prestige or a seal of distinction; originally the word meant an official seal.

clue.text: Land in East on time, I'm sure

parts.note: saying I bet means you are confident

explanation.surface: Someone confidently predicts landing in the East on schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: A Himalayan region of Asia, so a country in the East.

clue.text: Person with no faith or trust, initially, in a robbery

indicators.note: in places that letter inside the phrase a heist

parts.note: a heist is a robbery

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the word trust

explanation.surface: A person loses faith and trust after being caught up in a robbery.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who does not believe in any god holds no religious faith.

clue.text: A bit old, oddly, like most dailies today

indicators.note: oddly says the letters are arranged in a strange new order

explanation.surface: Modern newspapers are described as a little old-fashioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' looks like it picks odd letters, but it signals an anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Most modern newspapers are printed in the compact format, so this adjective describes them.

clue.text: Flourish report about learner

indicators.note: about means the word for a bang is placed around the letter

parts.note: a report is a loud bang, a boom
L is the learner sign, as on L-plates

explanation.surface: A favourable account about a student's progress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'report' looks like a school report, but it is the noise of a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: To thrive or prosper is to be in full flower, a synonym.

clue.text: Be insistent about property contract in statement to media

parts.note: to press is to urge insistently
re means about or concerning
a lease is a contract to rent property

explanation.surface: Someone presses hard about a tenancy deal in a public announcement.
explanation.definitionFit: An official announcement issued to journalists for publication.

clue.text: Literary types a university short changed

indicators.note: changed means the letters of short are rearranged

explanation.surface: Writers at a university were shortchanged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short changed' reads as cheated, but 'changed' scrambles SHORT into THORS.
explanation.definitionFit: Writers of books are literary people.

clue.text: Careful discussions with French composer as shareholder

indicators.note: holder means the composer's name holds the share inside it

parts.note: Léo Delibes was a French composer, of the ballet Coppélia
a ration is a fixed share

explanation.surface: Thoughtful talks involve a French composer who owns shares.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shareholder' reads as one word, but splits into 'share' and 'holder'.
explanation.definitionFit: Long, thoughtful consideration and debate before a decision.

clue.text: Watering-hole in sweltering Aussie city

indicators.note: in puts the pub word inside the heat word

parts.note: sweltering means very hot
a watering-hole is slang for a pub or bar

explanation.surface: A pub in a sweltering Australian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Hobart is the capital of the Australian state of Tasmania.

clue.text: As opposed to Nixon, for example, totally trustworthy

parts.note: UN is the prefix meaning not, the opposite
President Nixon faced impeachment proceedings, so he was open to that charge

explanation.surface: Unlike disgraced President Nixon, someone is completely honest.
explanation.definitionFit: Beyond reproach, so honest that no accusation could stick.

clue.text: Old hat's taken out by romantic

definitions.meaning: old hat means old-fashioned, no longer current
a suitor who takes someone out has gone on a date with them

explanation.surface: A battered old hat gets thrown out by a sentimental person.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both outmoded and having been escorted on an evening out.

clue.text: Banking can be corrupt I learnt

indicators.note: corrupt suggests these letters are spoilt into a different order

explanation.surface: Someone has learnt that banking can be crooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banking' looks like finance, but means depending, as in banking on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To be banking on something is to depend on it, so this adjective means depending.

clue.text: Starts off cutting hair in classic style

indicators.note: starts off picks the opening letter of each of the next four words

explanation.surface: A barber begins cutting hair in an elegant classic fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegance and fashionable stylishness, used as a noun.

clue.text: Opportunity to refuel car — mine's first

definitions.text: Opportunity to refuel car — mine's first

indicators.note: first says the mine word comes at the front

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine
a halt to fill up with fuel is a stop

explanation.surface: A driver claims first chance at the petrol pump.
explanation.definitionFit: In motor racing, a brief halt in the pits for fuel and tyres.

clue.text: Extremely bad in-house changes

indicators.note: changes says the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Office reorganisations are dreadful.
explanation.definitionFit: Shockingly wicked or evil, a strong synonym.

clue.text: Manage width and length (not all of it)

indicators.note: not all of it says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone copes with measurements, though not all of them.
explanation.definitionFit: To cope with or deal with something is to manage it.

clue.text: Humour about bishop's religious book collection

indicators.note: about puts the humour word around the letter

parts.note: bile was one of the four bodily humours of old medicine
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A joke about a bishop's library of holy books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Humour' means a bodily fluid, not comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: The scriptures are a collection of many sacred books in one volume.

clue.text: Work that's heavy, from my perspective

explanation.surface: In my view, this job is hard going.
explanation.definitionFit: A big heavy volume, and the phrase meaning in my view, written as one word.
